lens: The evidence pool lacks bound fact IDs, precluding citation-based theses; this analysis highlights discrepancies in optimal biomarker thresholds (e.g., vitamin D: >40 vs. >50 ng/mL) and treatment response variances (e.g., tamoxifen RR 10-53%) as potential research angles, emphasizing the need for targeted fact extraction.
known_to_ignore: Progestins are first-line hormonal therapy with a 25% response rate
Vitamin D serum levels above 40 ng/mL are vital for health
Tamoxifen response rates range from 10 to 53%
tensions: Optimal vitamin D levels conflict: some studies cite >40 ng/mL (paper=10.3390/nu16111666) while others recommend >50 ng/mL (125 nmol/L) for clinical outcomes
Hormonal therapy responses vary widely, e.g., tamoxifen RR 10-53% vs. aromatase inhibitors 8-9% in metastatic breast cancer
Heritable factors account for 60-80% of bone mineralization, but HRT optimization protocols often ignore genetic stratification
gaps: Underexplored subgroup: women with advanced liver disease, where amenorrhea prevalence >25% but hormone optimization strategies are lacking
Dose-specific gaps: optimal protein intake (1.4-2.2 g·kg⁻¹·day⁻¹) for menstrual function preservation in athletes not integrated with HRT
Timing gaps: impact of pregnancy-related cardiomyopathy (LVEF <45%) on postpartum hormone therapy efficacy and safety
reviewer_objections: Lack of direct evidence facts makes theses speculative; reliance on alpha hints violates citation rules
Tensions identified are based on single-paper assertions without cross-study validation, risking overgeneralization
Gaps proposed are inferred from hints, not empirical data, reducing methodological rigor
next_extractions: Extract facts on vitamin D RCTs with dose-response curves and subgroups like liver disease patients
Harvest data on hormonal therapy combinations (e.g., tamoxifen/progestin) with response rates stratified by PI3K/mTOR pathway alterations
Investigate studies linking protein intake interventions to menstrual cycle outcomes in HRT users
